conclusion.recommended: A separately typed B-owned companion retention-only group: explicit fixed B reservation plus canonical exact B root; C alone installs/debits the complete exact union. Keep B companion SQL absent during C preparation. After genuine C private AND family Ready, atomically insert B mappings/header/scalars/claim/receipt and CAS Staging->Ready, positively close and fresh-read, then use the existing Ready->Published protocol.
conclusion.schema_change: No DDL change proved necessary. Schema8 already contains required companion/receipt/content/claim tables; family schema2 already has reservations, roots and root_manifests. New payload/hash/funding-algorithm versions and named typed validation paths are required.
conclusion.b_quota: There is one family quota singleton, not spare per-B capacity. Existing B capture reservations are attempt-specific and cannot be borrowed. C plan.quota_bytes and its remaining belong to C exact installation/checkout even if proposal sizing includes some B SQL. Add an explicit B metadata-envelope reservation within unchanged family quota; refuse when free capacity cannot cover both. Never enlarge capture/C reservations or call set_quota.
conclusion.receipt_order_conflict: The proposal document says identical source/destination rows exist before EITHER receipt. The investigated hypothesis publishes B rows only AFTER C Ready, hence after C receipt. Both cannot hold. ROOT must explicitly adopt protect-both-before-either-receipt plus each-database-rows-before-its-own-receipt, or implement a different pending/Staging B SQL protocol. Recommendation selects the former; current documentation must change.
conclusion.no_completion_claim: This route supplies source ownership design only. Retained remote authority and genuine C companion-capable Ready/ordinary admission remain separate necessary integration.

evidence.fact: Receipt.companion_id FK requires header first; scalar companion_id requires header. No scalar FileId/ManifestId FK requires projection_content. Mapping requirement is an application contract. projection_content is FileId PRIMARY KEY; claim.kind/owner and family root/reservation operation are TEXT, allowing new typed classes without DDL.

ActivePublication still requires companion tables empty. It preflights transition/receipt relations, validates capture, then owns each receipt via one terminal source intent. It does not currently validate companion headers/scalars. Merely calling insert_new_rows in the writer cannot pass its own before/after validator.

Every content row must match a staged capture replacement; every claim must be provider-capture with unique staged owner. Accepted replacement/claim coverage is mandatory. Managed planning separately checks historical mapping cardinality against frozen prefix content_mappings. Extras cannot just be appended to PrivateCaptureProof.

Family B validation assigns ALL B reservations/roots to capture attempts, requires capture operations and caps capture remaining. Unknown B roots/reservations fail. require_no_owner_exact_installations also forbids B exact journals. A new B companion class must be explicitly accounted alongside capture, preserving owner completeness.

ExactProtection hardcodes provider-import:<transaction>, binds destination ExactBinding, and inspect/insert demands unique root for owner. B already has capture roots. Changing owner to B is not a valid use of protect_import. Keep its guards and add a separate SourceCompanionProtection type.

Incoming lineage begins at prefix.ancestry_root_receipt, follows parents and supplies scoped receipt/companion IDs. Content selectors use capture/incoming companion IDs, not whole tables. verify_source_publication separately binds outgoing rows while keeping the old closure. Its mode binding currently hashes only transition/receipt vectors; new companion proof must enter that equality/hash.

source_mappings prefers frozen mapping, else a companion file scalar. insert_new_rows/require_new_rows requires those mappings first on both databases. Scoped v2 authenticates scalar exact representation separately from unchanged sticky mapping, but still REQUIRES both and base/preimage mappings. Descriptor-only bases absent from frozen mappings and file scalars need complete derivation from validated baseline/preimage inventory or early refusal.

It accepts no closed companion/source-protection input and checks metadata against C remaining. This is the concrete source insertion integration point.

Usage includes all reservations.remaining and exact journal charges. design.union: Use the same full sorted exact manifest union U committed by plan.protected_manifests for the first B retention root. This conservatively retains live/fresh/historical/companion/preimage representations, including both ManifestIds for one FileId. It is not duplicate content debit; C remains the only installer.

new_records.SourceCompanionBinding: Family incarnation/root/catalog/marker IDs; B worktree/private DB/schema8; frozen prefix ID; transaction ID/immutable plan digest/companion ID/protected-manifest commitment; C owner/private DB/destination-proof digest; distinct deterministic B operation/reservation; funding algorithm v1.

mapping_rules: Preserve every existing sticky mapping exactly. Missing mappings may be inserted only from closed validated source reconciliation; never prefer an arbitrary alternate representation.

Capture proof keeps capture-only mappings/claims and all current Accepted coverage. The actual SQL set equals the union of capture-stage references and precisely validated terminal companion references; unknown extras fail.
Capture and companion may reference the same FileId and same unchanged SQL row. Later capture does not transfer ownership away from old companion; classify references, not disjoint FileId ownership.

All scalar files, bases, accepted preimages and satisfied-intent dependencies require their exact sticky mapping as current v2 specifies. The scalar alternate and sticky mapping must both belong to protected header/U.
Outgoing companion extras never join frozen source-prefix ContentMappings/Companions/TransitionReceipts selectors. Incoming ancestry stays unchanged.
funding_before_effects: Freeze closed source image/authority/closure, canonical companion rows, U, sticky mappings and Q_B/Q_C before reservation/installation/publication effects. Preflight every encoding, aggregate count and overflow first.
Q_C retains existing plan.quota_bytes meaning. Proposal counting B rows inside C metadata is conservative sizing, not B funding. Do not alter an already stored plan/reservation.

Use a deterministic versioned Q_B envelope from existing immutable rowsets and encoded bounds. Example mechanically safe v1: Q_B = M_B + 65536 + 256*|U| + 16MiB. The fixed 16MiB root maximum avoids a self-referential payload/amount sizing loop.

M_B covers source header/scalars, all required source mappings (charging reused rows too is conservative), one claim, source receipt and BOTH terminal source intent projections. Use bounded sizing-only serializers or conservatively 2*intent.MAX_BYTES plus receipt/header maxima and schema UTF-8 scalar bounds times committed counts. No fake valid records for sizing.

Refuse if M_B exceeds 1GiB, actual root exceeds 16MiB, header exceeds 65536, manifest/union bounds fail, or arithmetic exceeds SQLite integer range. MAX-payload sizing may reserve tens of MiB for small companions; this is an explicit conservative tradeoff, not silently expanded capacity.

Before first B/C reservation verify global usage + absent Q_B + absent Q_C <= unchanged family quota. Insert/replay fixed B reserve; C reserve still follows its existing legal phase and independently rechecks capacity. Separate commits may leave B reserved/C absent, safely blocked.

B reserve has remaining==Q_B throughout; no debit/release here. C alone charges new chunks/manifests/journals. SUM(remaining) includes B automatically. Validate actual source/root envelope before B root and every receipt/source writer open; never top up a persisted underfunded attempt.

No new plan field is logically necessary if Q_B is a deterministic function selected by new root/funding protocol and existing companion plan commitments. If ROOT wants separately serialized exact owner budgets, add a versioned plan record deliberately; that is optional API policy, not a proven DDL need.
steps: S0: existing B plan/Copying/Staging journal; no NEW B companion SQL rows, claim or receipt. Complete closed derivation and fixed envelopes.

S1: family transaction inserts exact B companion reservation linked to actual immutable B Staging plan; positive close/fresh read. Reservation-only gap is explicitly valid; arbitrary B reservations remain invalid.
S2: existing C member/reservation/exact install/debit protocol over U. Keep original B image pinned and B envelope fixed. Thread source-group context through family callbacks.

S3: after C U fully Published and independent CAS bytes verified outside SQL, insert B root+all root_manifests atomically in family transaction. Recheck B plan, C Published journals and B envelope. Exact absent-or-complete replay only; partial root refuses.

S4: C persists its mappings/header/scalars before C receipt, private Ready, then family Ready. Both independently owned roots/envelopes must pass before C receipt. Companion-capable Ready constructors must prove complete state; do not delete legacy refusal guards.

S5: with genuine C private+family Ready and both roots retained, open FK-enabled B writer. Authenticate original frozen prefix before extras. In ONE transaction insert absent exact B mappings; exact header/scalars; B claim; source receipt; Staging->Ready CAS; full prospective validation; COMMIT.
S5 acknowledgment: nested C/family RO positive closes, source writer positive close/ACK, then complete fresh B/C/family read. No further operation after uncertain close.
S6: retain existing separate Ready->Published CAS/close/fresh-read. No source byte rehash after B Ready. Root/reservation/mappings/rows/claim remain unchanged. Published replay is no-write.
phase_contracts: Staging allows exact reservation absent/present and exact root absent/present only in protocol order, but no private companion rows/claim/receipt. Root is already durably owned through actual source plan, not a private orphan adopted later.
Ready/Published require complete private companion projection and existing exact B root/reservation. Claim/header/scalars/mappings/receipt/Ready cannot commit separately.
Before source Ready failures rollback all B SQL together. After uncertain COMMIT/close return failure; next owner may recognize complete Ready and resume, but never repairs partial/corrupt rows/root.
B reservation-only/root-only/C-Ready-B-Staging crash states remain retained and resumable or blocked. No cleanup/release in this tranche.
Restart cannot turn root/SQL DATA into original native/remote authority. Reacquire genuine source/image/authority capabilities or a supported recovery owner before dependent operations.
C autonomous open uses C private receipt/claim/root and full union, with no B database/native/provider lookup. New B group classification must not impose B availability on C.
Keep current provider/admitted reclamation refusal. Future source removal/reservation release/GC needs a separate protocol for the new group.
